terms.definition: The extension of an object is proportional to the force applied, up to the limit of proportionality.
terms.examiner: F = kΔL. Say 'up to the limit of proportionality'.

terms.definition: The greatest force or stress after which the material does not return to its original length when the force is removed.
terms.examiner: Beyond it the deformation is plastic.

terms.definition: Force per unit cross-sectional area, F/A, in Pa.
terms.examiner: Use the original cross-sectional area; for a wire A = πd²/4.

terms.definition: Extension divided by original length, ΔL/L; no unit.
Tensile stress divided by tensile strain, in the region where Hooke's law applies.
terms.examiner: Gradient of the linear part of the stress–strain graph.

terms.definition: The maximum stress a material can withstand before it breaks.
terms.examiner: Also called ultimate tensile stress in some questions.

terms.definition: A material that breaks without significant plastic deformation, such as glass.
terms.examiner: Contrast with ductile (can be drawn into wires) and plastic behaviour.
